title: Annotatio V §.I: Limits opposite Obstacles — by right (jure), not merely de facto
pass_a_gloss: §. I. Limits, opposite to Obstacles, are understood of Right, as Obstacles are of fact. Just as an unjust boundary takes on the nature of an obstacle, so a just obstacle takes on the nature of a limit. Hence the limits of Ecclesiastical Consociation in this place are understood not such as are given in act and de facto, but such as by right — and indeed by Divine and Ecclesiastical right — both can and ought to be given.
pass_b_english: §. I. Limits stand opposite Obstacles: limits are understood of right, obstacles of fact.
An unjust boundary acts like an obstacle; a just obstacle acts like a limit.
So here the limits of church consociation are not whatever happens to obtain in practice, but what by divine and church right can and ought to be set.
source_text:
§. I.
Limites, Obicibus oppositi, intelliguntur de Jure, uti Obices de facto. Quemadmodum limes injustus, obicis, ita obex justus, limitis naturam induit. Hinc limites Consociationis Ecclesiasticae hoc loco intelliguntur, non quales actu & de facto dantur, sed quales jure, & quidem Divinô ac Ecclesiastico, dari & possent, & debent.
notes: §.I; jure vs facto; unjust limes / just obex.
